Estimation needs its own noise parameters, matching @sec-noise. Here they are
declared directly, consistent with the noise used to generate the data above:

```{r}
#| label: sim-noise-params
sim_noise_params <- tibble::tibble(
  antigen_iso = antibodies,
  nu = 0.5, # biological noise
  eps = 0, # measurement noise
  y.low = 1, # lower limit of detection
  y.high = 5e6 # upper limit of detection
)
```

The assay limits censor measurements outside its quantifiable range.
The `y.low` value is the lower limit of detection, $L$,
and `y.high` is the upper limit, $U$.
A result reported at or below $L$
establishes only that the response lies in the lower interval.
A result reported at or above $U$
establishes only that it lies in the upper interval.

Let $f_\lambda(y \mid a)$ and $F_\lambda(y \mid a)$
be the model-implied density and cumulative distribution
for a participant of age $a$,
including the antibody-kinetics distribution and both noise sources.
The intended noise-consistent likelihood contribution is

$$
\Lik_i(\lambda) =
\begin{cases}
F_\lambda(L \mid a_i), & y_i \le L, \\
f_\lambda(y_i \mid a_i), & L < y_i < U, \\
1 - F_\lambda(U \mid a_i), & y_i \ge U.
\end{cases}
$$

Thus, a threshold-reported result contributes
the probability of its entire censoring interval,
rather than the density at an arbitrarily substituted boundary value.

As implemented in `serocalculator` 1.4.1.9042
(verified 2026-08-25 on the package source),
measurement noise is included for uncensored and lower-censored observations
but is inadvertently omitted from the upper-censored contribution.
Issue [#664](https://github.com/UCD-SERG/serocalculator/issues/664)
tracks the correction needed to make that branch conform to the equation above.
